name: Dapagliflozin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: CKD at risk of progression; heart failure; cardiovascular risk in type 2 diabetes

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 5 mg once daily; may increase to 10 mg

key_interactions.action: Assess volume status and consider diuretic dose reduction; monitor kidney function.
Lower insulin or secretagogue doses may be needed.
Check lithium levels more often when starting or changing the dose.
Use other methods to monitor glycemic control.

common: Female genital mycotic infections, nasopharyngitis, urinary tract infections (≥5%)

contraindications: History of serious hypersensitivity to dapagliflozin or any excipient
monitoring: Kidney function before starting and as indicated
Ketones/ketoacidosis signs when acutely ill; withhold at least 3 days before surgery or prolonged fasting

pk.metabolism: Mainly UGT1A9 to inactive dapagliflozin 3-O-glucuronide; CYP minor
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 75% of radioactivity in urine (under 2% as parent); 21% in feces
pk.dialyzability: Unknown: removal by hemodialysis not studied (label).
